entries.test: Public financial evidence on generative AI businesses and reproducible research on whether their factual errors can be eliminated would test the claim.
entries.note: Assess profitability and technical limitations as of publication.

entries.test: Public technical research or a demonstrated generative AI system with general human-like cognition would test the asserted impossibility.
entries.note: This is Zitron's own impossibility assertion, distinct from OpenAI's reported ambition.

entries.test: Documentation and reproducible tests of Recall's publication-era handling of passwords, health information, and other sensitive content would settle this.
entries.note: Later changes to Recall do not establish its capabilities in June 2024.
Whether the risk is unacceptable is a judgment, distinct from whether the ICO investigated it.

entries.test: Publication-era product demonstrations, documented customer uses, and financial disclosures would show whether integrated AI offered new capabilities, met needs, or generated profit.
entries.note: The proposition preserves the author's 'seem' qualification.

entries.test: The Super Bowl advertisement and reproducible tests of the advertised Copilot version would show whether multiple depicted capabilities were unavailable.

entries.note: The surrounding passage supplies the growth motive. The misinformation examples are checkable separately, but the combined claim attributes a private motive.
The proposition converts a possible shortage of markets into an actual shortage and drops the tentative framing. Industry-wide desperation is an attributed mental state.
The embedded assertion is endorsed despite the rhetorical question. The impossibility clause is separately checkable, but the combined claim includes 'likely'.

entries.test: Public interviews and presentations by Altman, Pichai, and Nadella would show whether they explained useful current AI capabilities.
entries.note: The proposition generalizes from three named executives and strengthens the qualified description into categorical inability.
Documented uses can test the utility clause separately. The combined claim also attributes hopes to companies.

entries.test: Public explanations available at publication would show whether anyone articulated how and why generative AI could become a major technology market.
entries.note: The claim concerns the existence of an explanation, not whether its promised outcome occurred.
A compelling reason for daily use is evaluative. The proposition also expands the accuracy qualification from dataset queries to all outputs.
The source presents this diagnosis under 'the problem might ... be'; the proposition removes that uncertainty.
The core assertion concerns Altman's private reason for seeking the investment.
The passage says the industry 'might' have run out of ideas. The proposition adds a firm assertion that generative AI cannot fill the gap.
The product ranking is evaluative, and fraud is raised only as a possibility.

entries.test: Public sales pitches and contemporaneous product tests would show whether Altman and Lyu sold products whose capabilities fell short of their representations.
Dated public statements by Altman and Lyu, compared with demonstrated product capabilities, would test the alleged exaggerations and their frequency.
entries.note: The factual reading is repeated capability overstatement; 'shamelessly' adds an evaluative flourish.
This is a disparaging characterization rather than a defined professional qualification claim.

entries.test: A publicly documented breakthrough establishing generative AI's broadly transformative practical usefulness would falsify the forecast.
entries.note: The preceding questions identify what 'it' refers to; no deadline is supplied.

entries.test: Public evidence of major societal or economic transformation caused by generative AI, or by AI developed by OpenAI or Anthropic, would falsify the relevant denial.
entries.note: The denials are firm despite the separate concession that other AI might change the world.
'I imagine' frames the absorption scenario as conjecture rather than a firm prediction.

entries.test: Public technology valuations, financing flows, and hardware and software investment records would show a broad investment-bubble collapse and the billions invested before it.
entries.note: The prediction is unequivocal but supplies no deadline.

entries.test: Publicly documented contingency plans, financial reserves, and risk controls at major technology companies would test their preparedness for a technology-market collapse.
entries.note: The proposition removes 'I just don't think' and makes the statement categorical. Preparedness has a practical reading that public evidence can test.
